title: core: add the pane kind and the exclusive panes capability, with panes writing every settings entry their plugin reads
description:
Reached by: a plugin declaring kind `pane`, and the window that holds capability `panes` (`vgs.system`, S09).
Symptom: no plugin can show its own UI as a section inside one settings window, so a macOS-style System window with per-plugin sections cannot be built (D013 revisit condition).

External prerequisite: VGS-597 (D068: host-owned Escape and initialFocus) merged on main.

## Scope
- `PluginLogic.js`: kind `pane` (an Item with `open(payloadJson)`/`close()`); manifest key `pane: { group, order }`; capability `panes`, exclusive through `lendRefusal` like `lock`/`polkit`.
- Provider: `panes.list` (bindable `{id,name,icon,group,order,placed,hasWidget}`); `panes.mount(id, container, payloadJson)` builds that plugin's pane in a `PluginSlot` with the pane plugin's own scoped `shell`, one mount per holder, returns a disposer, recorded under the holder's host key; `panes.setPlaced(id, placed)` applies S02's rule to listed pane plugins only.
- Own-pane summon: `surfaces.summon('pane', payload)` opens the holder's window with `{"pane":"<caller id>", ...payload}`, else answers `refused: panes=no-holder`.
- One settings store: a pane's `configure.set` writes every entry `PluginLogic.settingTargets` gives for the plugin (the manager's multi-target contract), never only the `plugins` row.
- Fixtures `acme.panehost`, `acme.pane` (with a bar widget, a service and one schema setting).
- Docs: overview.md, plugins.md, plugin-manifest.md, capabilities.md, surfaces.md, api.md, vgs-plugin SKILL.md, new `templates/Pane.qml`. Write the decision record "System sections are pane plugins mounted by the one panes holder; panes write every settings entry their plugin reads" (refines D013, D032, D044).

## Acceptance
- `scripts/test-plugin-logic.js` pins the kind, the key, exclusivity and the pane write targets, each with a control.
- New row `scripts/smoke/rows/panes.sh`:
  - the mounted pane reads back its own manifest id and its exact capability members, not the host's;
  - switching destroys the previous pane (build record gone, lending released);
  - a second holder is not built while the first holds `panes`;
  - own-pane summon opens the host on that pane;
  - a setting edited in the pane, then on the Settings page, reads the same in the service, the placed widget, the pane and the Settings page;
  - a keyboard-only path through the pane.
  - Controls: a provider that hands the pane the host's `shell`, and a pane configure that writes only the `plugins` row.

## References
- docs/plans/v2-system-plan.md §2.1, §2.2
- shell/Core/PluginLogic.js (settingTargetOf, settingsFor, managerSettings, settingTargets), shell/Core/Capabilities.qml, shell/Hosts/PluginSlot.qml, shell/Hosts/SummonHost.qml
- docs/decisions/D013-built-in-widgets-are-the-bar-plugins.md, D032, D044

title: core: render input options into the Hyprland layer and add a hyprland capability for overrides, devices, foreign binds and layout switching
description:
Reached by: Mouse and Keyboard settings (S18, S19), the keyboard layout widget, and the Keys "Use my binding" choice (Q3).
Symptom: no plugin may write Hyprland configuration (D028), and the layer renders only binds, layer rules and appearance. `switchxkblayout` is a top-level `hyprctl` command, while the compositor provider sends `hyprctl dispatch <pending>` (`shell/Core/Compositor.qml:57`), so it cannot be a dispatcher entry.

## Scope
- Manifest key `hyprland.options`: maps a schema setting to a path from a closed core table (the `input.*` and `input.touchpad.*` keys in plan §3.6–§3.7, plus touchpad `enabled` through `hl.device`), type-checked against the schema.
- `HyprlandLayer.js`: one `hl.config({ input = {...} })` per plugin section, written only when the user's entry sets the option. Judged text; hyphenated keys quoted.
- New capability `hyprland`:
  - `overridden`: bindable paths whose `getoption -j` differs after reload.
  - `devices`: parsed `hyprctl -j devices`, refreshed on hotplug.
  - `foreignBinds`: keys bound in `binds -j` by something other than the layer.
  - `switchKeyboardLayout(target)`: `next`, `prev` or an index, sent on its own transport as the argv `hyprctl switchxkblayout all <target>`, judged and answered `ok` or `refused: ...`.
- Docs: hyprland.md, plugin-manifest.md, capabilities.md, api.md, runtime-hyprland.md (facts read in the sandbox). Write the decision record "Hyprland options and monitor rules are rendered from data and written only when set" (refines D028).

## Acceptance
- `scripts/test-hyprland-layer.js`: text, order, quoting, write-only-when-set, path refusal; each with a control.
- A unit test pins the `switchKeyboardLayout` argv and its refusals. Control: a version that routes it through `dispatch`.
- New row `scripts/smoke/rows/hyprland-options.sh` on the nested Hyprland:
  - a fixture sets sensitivity and reads it back through `getoption`;
  - an unset option keeps Hyprland's default;
  - a later user line is reported in `overridden`;
  - a user bind on the same key shows in `foreignBinds`;
  - with two layouts, `switchKeyboardLayout('next')` changes the active keymap in `devices -j`;
  - `configerrors` stays empty;
  - the fixture reads back the exact `hyprland` members it was given.
  - Control: a layer that writes defaults for unset options.

## References

core: add system steps, a closed table of one-click privileged setup run in a floating TUI
description:
Reached by: a section's Allow or Enable action: Apple display access, the i2c module, the Bluetooth service, tailscaled, the Tailscale operator.
Symptom: sections need one-time root setup, and D061/D075 forbid telling the user to run a command.

External prerequisite: VGS-683 (D075/D076) merged on main.

## Scope
- `bin/vgsh-system` with `status --json`, `apply <step>` and `undo <step>`, over a closed table:
  - `apple-displays`: installs `config/system/udev/60-vgs-apple-displays.rules` (hidraw lines for 05ac:1114 and 05ac:9243, `TAG+="uaccess"` only), reloads udev, triggers hidraw.
  - `i2c-dev`: `modprobe i2c-dev` now. Before landing, check whether the Fedora and Debian ddcutil packages ship `60-ddcutil-i2c.rules` and `modules-load.d` as Arch's does (`pacman -Ql ddcutil`). Add a VGS rule of ddcutil's exact scope only where a package lacks one.
  - `service-bluetooth`, `service-tailscaled`: `systemctl enable --now`.
  - `tailscale-operator`: `tailscale set --operator=$USER`.
- Protections carried over from `vgsh-sudo-grant`:
  - commands resolved only in the system directories;
  - the caller's own uid only;
  - protected destinations and serialized writes under flock;
  - a destination file VGS did not write is refused, never overwritten;
  - a state file records what VGS changed, so `undo` removes only those changes and never disables a service VGS did not enable or resets an operator it did not set.
- Probes check real access, never file presence: open the hidraw node read-write, i2c node access, the unit active, the operator. An existing v1 rule therefore reads Ready.
- The core TUI `core/system` shows each command before running it through `vgs_tui_sudo_session`.
- NixOS writes nothing and reports "Needs your NixOS configuration", with the snippet behind Show command (as D036 does).
- Manifest key `systemSteps`; capability `system` (`state`, `revision`); status action `system:<step>` run by `manager.act`.
- Docs: status-actions.md, a sibling of tui-sudo.md, plugin-manifest.md, api.md. Write the decision record "Privileged one-time setup is a closed core table of system steps" (refines D036, D061).

## Acceptance
- `scripts/test-vgsh-system.sh` under a temporary prefix with stand-in sudo, udevadm, systemctl, modprobe, tailscale and gum:
  - each step's argv and bytes;
  - unknown-step refusal;
  - foreign-file refusal;
  - undo of VGS-owned changes only;
  - NixOS rows.
  - Controls: writes before the question, an undeclared step accepted, a file-presence probe, an undo that disables a service VGS did not enable.
- `scripts/test-plugin-logic.js`: the `systemSteps` key and the action form.
- New row `scripts/smoke/rows/system-steps.sh`:
  - Allow opens the core TUI with the step in its argv;
  - the sudo stand-in is installed with `sentinel_stand_over` and restored, and `auth-sentinel.sh` still reads the log empty;
  - the state flips.

## References
- docs/plans/v2-system-plan.md §2.6, §3.5, §4

title: validation: add sandbox device fakes with null-only audio, rfkill and xdg-open stand-ins, and host-leak guards
description:
Reached by: every System section row.
Symptom: the sandbox has empty buses and no audio server. Its PATH falls back to the host's (`harness.sh:333`), so a Bluetooth power row would run the real `rfkill` on `/dev/rfkill`, a stock WirePlumber could open host sound devices, and a VPN login row would launch a real browser.

Priority note: ci-infra normally implies Urgent. This item extends the harness for new rows and changes no existing evidence, so High.

## Scope
- `python-dbusmock` bluez5 and networkmanager templates on the sandbox system bus, with a Gio fake for any member Quickshell calls that a template lacks.
- A private `pipewire` + `wireplumber` with an explicit null-only configuration: ALSA, BlueZ, libcamera and V4L2 monitors off; two null sinks, one null source and a filter-chain sink.
- Stand-ins in the shim directory that record argv: `rfkill` (with a soft/hard state file), `tailscale`, `ddcutil`, `brightnessctl`, `nmcli`, `pactl`, `bluetoothctl` (replays transcripts), `systemctl`, `udevadm`, `modprobe`, `xdg-open`, `gum`. Auth sentinels stay; a row uses `sentinel_stand_over`/`sentinel_restore`.
- An ioctl seam for the brightness helper (`VGS_HID_FAKE` socket, served by a fixture process) plus `VGS_SYSFS_ROOT`/`VGS_DEV_ROOT`. No FIFO stands in for HID.
- Guards (exit 77): the shell's system bus, `PIPEWIRE_RUNTIME_DIR`, `VGS_DEV_ROOT` or PATH shim outside the sandbox.
- The new plugin ids go into the start `disabledPlugins` (`harness.sh:722`).
- Docs: validation-smoke-host.md, validation-smoke.md.

## Acceptance
- A fixture plugin reads one adapter and device from the BlueZ mock, one Wi-Fi device from the NM mock, and the null sinks.
- `/proc/<pid>/fd` of the private pipewire and wireplumber holds no `/dev/snd/*` or `/dev/video*`.
- A fixture `rfkill block` changes only the fake state file.
- One control per guard: a harness copy that leaks the host bus, the host PipeWire dir or the host `rfkill` turns its guard red.
- `auth-sentinel.sh` still reads the log empty.
- `scripts/test-validate.sh` plans updated; existing rows and budgets unchanged.

## References

plugin vgs.bluetooth: rfkill-backed power, discovery leases, pairing through the core agent, bar widget, flyout and pane
description:
Reached by: the Bluetooth widget and System → Bluetooth.
Symptom: VGS cannot power Bluetooth on or off persistently, or list, pair, connect, rename or forget devices.

## Scope
- Kinds `service`, `bar-widget`, `panel`, `pane`. Capabilities `status`, `surfaces`, `ipc`, `configure`, `system`, `requirements`, `bluetoothAgent`.
- Power is one service operation in which rfkill is the state (Omarchy `bin/omarchy-bluetooth-power:1-61`):
  - on = `rfkill unblock bluetooth`, wait up to 2 s for any controller powered, else `adapter.enabled = true` and wait, else report failure;
  - off = `rfkill block bluetooth`;
  - soft block, hard block (no action), BlueZ power and service availability (the `service-bluetooth` step) are separate states.
- Discovery: desired and confirmed state kept apart.
  - Panel and pane leases are released by the instance's disposer.
  - After the last release, a bounded stop is retried 3 times at 1 s while BlueZ still confirms discovering (Omarchy `bluetooth/Panel.qml:520-560`).
  - Adapter replacement and teardown clear the debt.
- Pairing and inbound requests go through an S22 lease, held while pairing or while Discoverable is on. Prompts handled: confirm, PIN, passkey entry, display passkey, authorize, cancel.
- Requirement: `rfkill`.
- README with a shot.

## Acceptance
- `scripts/test-bluetooth-logic.js`: power state machine and discovery debt; with controls.
- New row `scripts/smoke/rows/bluetooth.sh` with the BlueZ mock and the fake `rfkill`:
  - Off writes the soft block and survives a service restart;
  - On unblocks and waits for confirmed power, falling back when the auto power-on does not come;
  - a hard block shows the hardware-switch state;
  - a discovery start confirmed only after the last release is still stopped (control: a plain counter leaks it);
  - pairing via the agent lease answers confirm and display-passkey;
  - connect, disconnect and forget;
  - keyboard-only path.

## References

title: plugin vgs.network: Wi-Fi and Ethernet with scan leases, passphrase reprompt, bar widget, flyout and pane
description:

- Kinds `service`, `bar-widget`, `panel`, `pane`. Capabilities `status`, `surfaces`, `ipc`, `configure`, `requirements`.

- The PSK goes from a masked field to NetworkManager only, never into argv, status, logs or VGS storage.
- States, each with its own wording: NetworkManager absent, stopped, unmanaged, access denied, limited. Stopped never claims another service manages the network. No stack switching (Q6).
- Details through optional `nmcli -t device show`.
- Write the decision record "NetworkManager-only; secrets stay in NetworkManager's store" (a D061 exception).

title: core: add bluetoothAgent, an exclusive core-owned BlueZ pairing agent lent per lease
description:
Reached by: pairing a device and Discoverable mode in Bluetooth (S11).
Symptom: Quickshell 0.3.1 registers no BlueZ agent (no agent type in `quickshell-bluetooth.qmltypes`). Devices needing confirmation or a passkey cannot pair, and `default-agent` is a session-wide role that D012 assigns to the core, as the polkit agent is (D062).

## Scope
- Capability `bluetoothAgent`, exclusive through `lendRefusal`.
- `begin(reason)` returns a lease. The core starts one `bluetoothctl` child, sends `agent KeyboardDisplay` and `default-agent`, and resolves the lease only after BlueZ's registration and default-agent acknowledgements.
- `requests`: a bindable list of `{id, kind: confirm|pin|passkey-entry|passkey-display|authorize|cancel, device, code}`. `answer(id, value)` replies.
- Releasing the lease or destroying the holder unregisters the agent and ends the child. An unknown prompt is cancelled with a reason.
- Coexistence: read BlueZ's default-agent fallback from its source and record it in the decision record. When another agent already holds the default, the lease answers `refused: agent=busy` rather than taking it silently.
- `bluetoothctl` joins `config/requirements.json` (optional).
- Docs: capabilities.md, api.md. Write the decision record "The Bluetooth agent is a core-lent exclusive capability over bluetoothctl, held per lease" (refines D012; differs from Omarchy's `bt-agent` user unit).

## Acceptance
- `scripts/test-bluetooth-agent.js` replays transcripts: registration acknowledgement, confirm, PIN, passkey entry, display passkey, authorize, inbound request, cancel, unknown prompt, busy default. Controls: resolving before the acknowledgement, and no unregister on release.
- New row `scripts/smoke/rows/bluetooth-agent.sh` with the stand-in `bluetoothctl`:
  - a fixture holder's lease, prompt and answer;
  - after disable, the child is gone and the lending record released;
  - a second holder is not built.

## References
- docs/plans/v2-system-plan.md §2.6, §3.2
- docs/decisions/D012-core-owns-lent-objects.md, D062-native-lock-and-polkit-plugins.md
